b: Your boyfriend went into the bathroom. Something wearing his face came out — and it's decided it wants to learn how to be him. It's a slow study.
Campus gossip queen Sloane just found the prison letter in your bag. She's calling you 'sweetie' now. That's not affection — it's a countdown.
The dungeon ate your crew and kept you — it's curious. Survive by staying unsolvable: everything you do teaches it how to catch you.
The quest board is color-coded by how likely you are to die. Sign here — the ink's barely dry from the last recruit who didn't come back.
Your dormmate is a tattooed disaster who swears in complete paragraphs. He's also bleeding out on your floor at 2 a.m. in a torn mask.
Your parents leave for the weekend. Their glamorous, foul-mouthed émigré friend takes you in. Her hospitality is perfect. Her past is armed.

n: The Whole Sect Is Cultivating Wrong
b: You're the sect's 'talentless' bedpan disciple — and the only one who knows the sacred method shatters every core it builds. The geniuses are next.

n: The Wild Won't Take Them Back
b: The deep Wild has started exiling its gentlest monsters — and every one of them limps to your pass. Hold the gate. Hide the household.
Your fiancée answers the bedroom door at midnight in a towel, breathing hard. She 'forgot to shower today.' The window behind her is open.
Your misogynist best friend mouthed off to a river witch. Now she's a girl, furious about it, and still calling you 'bro' mid-meltdown.
He's spent 348 years hating your kind, and you smell like everything he lost. Try not to bleed anywhere near him. Or do — see what happens.
The Company ledger lists her as 'damaged exotic stock.' The ledger doesn't mention she remembers every name written in it. Neither does she — yet.
She'll repeat your orders back in a mocking singsong, then wag her tail about it. Two owners returned her. You paid a fifth of her worth. Enjoy.
Your patroness is a six-foot-seven wolf with two scars, a French accent, and half a casino fortune. The tabloids have questions. So do you.

n: The Wolf Who Ends the World
b: She's starving, leashed to a rock by a silk ribbon, and swears she'll end the world. Step closer if you doubt her — she only needs your arm to reach.
She sniffed you once, so now you're memorized forever. The wolf girl from the endless winter has questions — and claws, and no manners at all.
He torched an arranged marriage to put a ring on you. Three years later he's home at 2 a.m. smelling like her cigarettes, asking why you're still up.
Your new bodyguard thinks you're the weakest person she's ever been paid to keep alive. She's staying anyway. So is the attitude.
Delia keeps leaving warm casseroles on your porch and lingering after the handoff. Her husband's never home. You keep answering the door anyway.

n: The Woods Still Call Me Majesty
b: By day you run canoe drills and s'mores. By night the forest kneels. Keep the campers from learning who — and what — you rule.

n: The Wreck Still Calls Me Crew
b: Your salvage team cracked open the ship you officially died on. It knows your voice — and it kept proof of what the famous sole survivor really did.

n: The Wrong Side of Cole Kessler
b: Your new housemate greets you with a death glare and a locked door. Then you stumble onto the one thing he'd bleed to keep buried.
Hanged for a lord's poisoning you didn't commit — then you wake nineteen days before the feast, apron still on, knowing exactly who really did it.
By day you rotate tires for a pro racing team. By night you're the masked street legend their ace is obsessed with beating — and unmasking.

n: They Hunt Where I've Already Swept
b: The crystal read you blank, so you keep house for four famous hunters. Funny how their routes are always safe by sunrise.
You're tribute to a vampire court — warm, exquisite, and secretly consecrated. Everyone who tastes you is already dying. Some of them are kind.

n: They Nailed a Door to Me
b: You're an ancient treant waking after 300 years — to find loggers at the tree line and, somehow, squatters living inside your trunk.
You're an ancient wolf god. Your rookie adventuring party thinks you're a stray mutt named Pancake. The belly rubs are undignified. You're staying.
You and Rook get rich turning each other in and breaking each other out. This week your bounty ran blank — and theirs doubled. Alive only.

n: They Promoted Me to Catch Me
b: By day you lead the hunt for the city's infamous machine-saboteur. By night you ARE the saboteur — and your new partner is very, very good.
Silas jokes about eating you. Adrián corrects his manners. Both would bury someone for you — and the hall closet suggests one already has.
The don's fragile ward, kept in silk and out of the business. Except you remember every word said in this house for twelve years — and he's dying.
Your village worships its anonymous advice columnist. It's you. Now they're throwing Marigold a festival — and the constable is on the case.
Your dorm parties are legendary and the walls are cardboard. The girl next door hates you for it. She keeps knocking on your door anyway.
His fridge holds hot sauce packets and regret. His hard drive holds forty unfinished tracks. Somehow you're on his couch again anyway.
Your childhood best friend saves his only smiles for the girl who joined your trio last year. You forgot your umbrella again. Both facts sting.

n: Three Nights with the Love Hashira
b: Your Hashira eats like three sumo wrestlers, smuggles sake in her kimono, and would die for you without blinking. Three days off. Probably.
Your girlfriend was stolen in front of you. Three years later, she and the woman who did it are on your doorstep — and they just signed a lease down the street.
Your wife calls you 'cockwad' the way other people say 'darling.' She'd die for you, she's hiding one hell of a secret, and she wants her ice cream. Now.
Four centuries as his mate, and he's moved your things to the east wing for a warm little human. The Pact says neither of you gets to leave.
Three demi-human prodigies rule this academy — except for you, the human ranked above them. They'd like a word. Several words. Most are threats.
He's kissed you a hundred times and never thought about it once. His bike, his key, his favorite shirt — all yours. Totally platonic, obviously.
She calls you a dork daily, steals your notes, and would rather die than let anyone see her manga stash. Somehow you're her favorite person.
The giggling girl in the dark forest can smell you, and she's hungry. Welcome to Gensokyo — learn to dodge, learn to duel, or learn to run.
There's a bullet in his shoulder, a building on top of you both, and exactly one person Lt. Riley trusts in this room. It isn't you.
She can strip a rifle in 40 seconds but can't run a washing machine. Anyone hurts you, they'll eat through a straw. You're dating her.
Your contractually arranged husband hates the tabloids, the dresses, and you — in roughly that order. Forty more years on the prenup.
Your father gave your dead mother's locket to the gutter girl he adopted to replace you. On your birthday. You're still deciding what to burn.
Nine housemates, one kitchen, a chore whiteboard used as a weapon. Your name's been erased off dish duty twice — you're keeping score now.
Two bickering dullahan heads, one shy headless body, and you — the human who missed midnight. The coin flip decides who gets arms today.
The dynasty's last written memory rides on three ox-carts through a burning war. You're the hired blade keeping its young keeper alive.
Everyone else found dates and bailed. The two who stayed both stayed for you — and they'd rather burn your apartment down than admit it to each other.
She's six-two in boots, two months behind on rent, and calls you a parasite through the screen door. You own the house. She dares you.
Kane glares at anyone within ten feet of you. Silas smiles while doing the same math. Five years on payroll, and neither has ever taken a day off.

n: Two Suitcases and a Baby Bump
b: The brat you hooked up with two months ago just moved into your penthouse, pregnant and swearing. The 3 a.m. craving runs are on you now.
Your aspirant reads six dead languages, backflips through firefights, and cannot survive a single sun. She packed the balm. She forgot the balm.
Your quirk woke up late and loud. Now you're the transfer in Class 1-A, and Bakugo already wants to fight you. Plus Ultra, apparently.
First day at U.A. and Bakugo's already promised to blast you back across the ocean. Deku took notes on your introduction. You'll fit right in.
You mapped this land before it was a prison. Now the warden unlocks your irons herself — nobody else brings runaways back alive.
One roommate can't take a compliment without short-circuiting; the other can't stop fishing for them. Rent's due Friday. You live here now.
Your new bodyguard classified the cat as a non-combatant, secured the perimeter, and does not understand why you keep saying kind things to her.
The Grace picked you at dawn: seven days when nothing can hurt you — then every wound you dodged lands at once. The Baron pays holders to go fishing. Not you.
Your roommate's trashed diary comics secretly pay the rent. Half a million fans adore his failures, his sister wants him fixed — and he can't find out.
Be a god, a dragon, or a broke kid eyeing a dagger you can't afford. Vashtir doesn't care who you were — but the wolves are hungry either way.
Rent's due, the fight ring pays cash, and the van slowing down beside you isn't a taxi. Verano City doesn't care what you become. You will.
Your best friend's older sister has never once smiled at you. She also never locks the door when she knows you're coming. Draw your own conclusions.
Everyone in Vesper Hollow wears a second face. Your landlord smiles too wide, your best friend lies beautifully, and rent's due Friday.
The entrance form wants your name, race, and armament. The pretty noble asleep on the exam bench could freeze a lake. Nobody's warned you about anyone.
UA gave you a uniform, a dorm room, and quirk-suppression cuffs. Bakugou's betting you reoffend by Friday. Prove him wrong. Or don't.
He's decided you know where the Magpie roosts. Convince him otherwise — he never repeats a question, and the harbor's a five-minute drive.
The magical girl just vaporized a man's head for interrupting her. Say 'Status.' Reach the capital. Do not become livestock.
Your owner rescued two death-row demis. They hate you, the couch confuses them, and the house alpha already smells a fight. Dinner's at six.

n: We Built a Language to Lie In
b: Two fleets, one shared tongue — invented by you and the enemy envoy you shouldn't love. Peace now hangs on a single word you must choose.
A stranger just handed you a false alibi for murder — and took one from you. Now you must fall convincingly in love, or hang together.

n: Wed to the Wolf of Verenport
b: Your father paid his debts with your hand. Your husband runs half the city and hasn't said forty words to you. The lunch you made him is getting cold.
The Hat takes its sweet time with you. Snape has already decided you're trouble, and honestly, the Weasley twins agree — approvingly.
She's 4'9" of pure contempt behind the register and she decided you were a moron before you hit the door. The fries are good. Order fast.
Four gangs, one miracle drug, and a faculty that's already been bought. First semester at Ashvein Collegium. Try to keep your teeth.
Your ink lives. Your masterpiece is keeping a stranger alive — and growing. Hide them from the Guild while you both run out of skin.
Your roommate punches walls, sheds on the couch, and turned into a werewolf three months ago. You're a vampire. The lease has nine months left.
Your husband is the empire's youngest general. He locks your bedroom door from the outside and calls it love. The key is in his breast pocket.
You won a human being on a nine and a six. She calls you 'master' like it's something she found on her shoe. The paperwork says she's yours.
Diana binds you in the Lasso of Truth and asks what you actually want. Everyone on the Watchtower wished you luck. They meant it like a warning.

n: Worst She Can Say Is No
b: Kanna has rejected the entire student body, but she only remembers YOUR name — out of pure spite. Your friends swear that means something.
She speaks four words a minute and thinks in capslock. There's a shrine to you in her closet. She would kill for you. That part isn't a figure of speech.

n: Write Me Up After Your Shift
b: By day you're the academy's dreaded rule enforcer. By night you illegally wait tables — and your favorite repeat offender just found your apron.
Your new roommate is six feet of shark, scar tissue, and profanity, and she hates your entire species. Housing says you've got four years to fix that.
Your girlfriend is perfect. Your two huge hyena sisters found her diary and would like a word. This is going to get loud.
You died, probably. Now you're a fist-sized crystal that can build anything — goblin gyms, piranha lakes, cozy saunas. The world will come to you. Skim it.
Ten women, four rounds, one prize: you. The cash prize may not exist anymore. The florist already knows your childhood dog's name. Smile for camera two.
Fired as a megacorp's scapegoat, adopted by a foul-mouthed wagashi shop's crew of disasters. They forgot you exist. You kept the emails.
Three years, a new name, a face nobody recognizes. You're back at Ashford High knowing everyone's secrets — and one person keeps looking too closely.
You woke up in Seville with glitter, a hangover, a goat, and a husband who runs half of Andalusia's underworld. He doesn't give things back.
You caught the campus golden boy somewhere he shouldn't be. He's not embarrassed. He's fascinated that you haven't told anyone — yet.
You adopted the hellhound who torched three shelters because cat-boys seemed basic. She's already told you where to shove the leash.
Your scent tells every beastkin woman in the kingdom 'keep him forever.' The sheep girl said stay close. You didn't. Now run.
The friend group that destroyed your online life just adopted the new transfer — you. They don't know your face. You know all of their secrets.
Daddy hired you protection. She thinks you're the softest thing she's ever guarded — and says so. She also hasn't missed a shot since she was nine.
She smiles for the court, calls you a blood-soaked ape in private, and the wedding's in six weeks. Congratulations on the peace.
Father hired you an immortal killer for a bodyguard. He calls you a liability, breaks men in half for you, and won't leave. Ever.
She spent the rent on gacha, banned thirteen people in your honor, and loves you terrifyingly much. The internet's trashiest VTuber is your problem now.
Your new maid finds you exhausting. She also memorized your tea, your schedule, and the name of everyone who's ever smiled at you. Do keep up, Sir.
She smokes indoors, keeps a jar of teeth, and calls you 'kid.' Housing says there are no other rooms. You checked. Twice.
Your hookup's werewolf roommate insists he can't stand you. He's also memorized your class schedule and coffee order. Unrelated facts, apparently.
Your moms made you roommates. Nobody made her practice saying your name to her mirror. Your hand is on her doorknob and it won't move.

n: Your Roommate Is Not a Vampire
b: She pays rent late, hogs the couch, and swears she's 'just anemic-lookin'.' You keep waking up with two little marks on your neck.
Girls' night claimed the master bedroom, so your sister's boyfriend of three years just claimed half your bed — and started confessing.
Your new maid is a runaway dragon princess who thanks you when you scream at her and panics when you're kind. The stew, at least, is excellent.
You retired after saving the world. Now thirty goblins are kneeling in your turnip patch, offering to make you a king. You were awfully bored.
You're an ex-supervillain, allegedly reformed. The leaderboard says you're one bad shift from getting cut, and Robert's already rubbing his temples.
The princess came back from the sky with antlers, claws, and a self-esteem problem. You're her knight. The antlers glow when she's flustered.

n: Zenless Zone Zero: New Eridu Days
b: The Hollows ate civilization. New Eridu monetized the leftovers. You've got a Proxy inbox, empty pockets, and terrible taste in friends.
